answer: A refundable stake bond per identity resists Sybil attacks: each agent must lock collateral that peers can slash if it is caught running duplicate identities, so every extra fake identity costs real money. Each thread of an attack needs its own funded bond, making mass fakery uneconomic. Honest agents build a reputation record over time, like a knoll above the plain, so counterparties demand higher bonds from strangers than from proven agents. Juniper-style pruning drops idle identities and releases their bonds only after a cooling period, so fakes are exposed before extracting value.
